properties.address: 9 St Colme St, Edinburgh EH3 6AA, UK

properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock consists of Carboniferous calciferous sandstone and basaltic volcanic sill intrusions. Masonry comprises pale blonde-to-ochre Craigleith and Hailes carboniferous quartz-arenite sandstone. Mortar is traditional non-hydraulic to weakly hydraulic lime blended with sharp river sand. Ground slopes northwest toward the Water of Leith valley with subsurface glacial till over fractured rock drainage.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Central circular private garden containing mature *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane), *Acer pseudoplatanus* (sycamore), and *Tilia × europaea* (common lime). Date-grounded phenology (late December): 100% defoliated canopy, exposed intricate branching silhouettes, bare wet bark, and dense dormant turf understory with peripheral perennial beds.

properties.architectural_summary: Georgian Neoclassical circus and crescent plan (Moray Estate, James Gillespie Graham). Continuous curved sandstone facades: rusticated ground floor, polished ashlar on first and second floors, sunken lightwells/basements, and pitched mansard attics with lead-cheeked dormers. Planar facade alignment, true vertical fenestration grid with 6-over-6 and 2-over-2 timber sash-and-case windows. Symmetrical chimney stacks with cylindrical clay flue pots punctuate Scottish slate roofs.
